task.title: P6-002: Make same-type resource payloads echo their request and reject mismatches
task.description:
Migrated from specs/TODO-Phase-6.md (Stage 3 — Leverage: fixes that retire a whole class). Original id: P6-002. Size: M. Specs: specs/app-ui.md, specs/ui-work-loop.md.

**Make same-type resource payloads echo the request they answered, and have the consumer reject a mismatch and refetch()** (absorbs P6-014). The cross-shape class is closed (named-field payloads + deny_unknown_fields), but two resources of the same payload type can still swap payloads. Two live pairs: AllCardsPayload (/my and /my/all) and CollectionListPayload (destination.rs + move_selection.rs).

**MEASURED 2026-08-11 (maintainer ruling: hardening deferred while not exposed):** npm run diag:resource-ids plus a purpose-built same-type probe (/my/all?q=canary → SPA-nav to /my) both landed on fresh slots — real fetch fired, correct rows rendered. The historical flood technique found ZERO collisions across ~2,000 injected ids (previous largest recorded margin was ~50–66 slots) — the app has grown enough shell/tree resources that today's margin is enormous, though it remains an accident of layout, not a design. RE-MEASURE before dismissing this task again, and IMPLEMENT if exposure returns (a big resource-count refactor or upstream leptos changes could shrink the margin silently). The durable fix is upstream (P6-013, also deferred). Measurement session note: the diag required patching baseURL 127.0.0.1→localhost due to the Neon Auth trusted-origin issue filed separately.

Re-measured 2026-08-12 on main @99de608 (per the maintainer's re-measure-before-dismissing condition): structural audit found the same two same-type groups as July (AllCardsPayload /my<->/my/all — the only meaningful pair; CollectionListPayload — benign, identical zero-arg fetch, cross-decode returns identical correct data). Numeric probe rerun (diag:resource-ids + rebuilt q=canary same-type SPA probe, 2000-slot flood + no-flood control): ZERO collisions, margin unchanged; /my fired a real fetch post-nav, no canary leak. The margin remains an accident of layout, not a design — the mechanism fix is upstream (P6-013, parked). DISMISSED on this evidence: pure hardening against a twice-measured-unexposed risk.
